# Satipaṭṭhāna Saṁyutta (SN 47)

**ID:** SN 47
**Section:** Saṁyuttanikāya (sn)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-1
**Title (Pali):** Satipaṭṭhāna Saṁyutta
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0305m.mul2.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Satipaṭṭhāna Saṁyutta* (SN 47) is the forty-seventh section of the *Saṁyuttanikāya*, situated within the fifth major division (*Mahāvagga*) alongside collections on the other sets of aids to enlightenment (*bodhipakkhiyā dhammā*) [Bodhi 2005]. It comprises discourses centered on the four establishments or foundations of mindfulness (*satipaṭṭhāna*): contemplation of the body, feelings, mind, and dhammas (principles or causality). Unlike the extensive analytical expositions found in the *Satipaṭṭhāna Sutta* (MN 10) and *Mahāsatipaṭṭhāna Sutta* (DN 22), the discourses in this Saṁyutta typically present the four contemplations in brief outline, emphasizing mindfulness as a factor leading directly into meditative immersion and absorption (*jhāna*) rather than specialized insight techniques [Anālayo 2003; Anālayo 2010; Bodhi 2005].

 DharmaNexus matches corroborate these correspondences, registering multiple high-scoring cross-language alignments with Chinese *Saṁyuktāgama* fascicles (T 99), the Sanskrit *Mahāparinirvāṇasūtra*, and Śamathadeva's Tibetan *Abhidharmakośaṭīkopayikā* (D4094) [DharmaNexus]. Within the Pali canon, DharmaNexus detects widespread formulaic text reuse between SN 47 and closely related collections, most notably the *Anuruddha Saṁyutta* (SN 52), the *Mahāparinibbāna Sutta* (DN 16), the *Saḷāyatana Saṁyutta* (SN 35), and other wings of the *Mahāvagga* [DharmaNexus].
